bugs.summary: try() errors when parsing an invalid pipe statement

comments.text:
```
try(parse(text = "f |> g"))
# Error in call[[1L]] : object of type 'symbol' is not subsettable
```

As reported to {lintr}: https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/issues/3038
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
This works:

```
Index: src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R   (revision 90558)
+++ src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R   (working copy)
@@ -27,7 +27,7 @@
             ## try(stop(...)).  This will need adjusting if the
             ## implementation of tryCatch changes.
             ## Use identical() since call[[1L]] can be non-atomic.
-            if (identical(call[[1L]], quote(doTryCatch)))
+            if (!is.symbol(call) && identical(call[[1L]], quote(doTryCatch)))
                 call <- sys.call(-4L)
             dcall <- deparse(call, nlines = 1L)
             prefix <- paste("Error in", dcall, ": ")
```

with updated behavior:

```
try(parse(text='f|>g'))
# Error in g : 
#   The pipe operator requires a function call as RHS (<text>:1:4)
```

There's a bit of a gray area here, though, as `conditionCall()` in general expects the `$call` component of the error object to be, well, a call.

`raiseParseError()` is passing `g` to the call slot here:

https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/blob/036fc467d199bfa10fb8ba6c37a930fe9fa9991a/src/main/gram.y#L1269-L1270

`g` is appearing where syntactically there _should_ be a call, but the parser should assume it's just a symbol -- so an approach of coercing `rhs` to a call for the error object feels off.

Another possibility is this:

```
Index: src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R
===================================================================
--- src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R   (revision 90558)
+++ src/library/base/R/New-Internal.R   (working copy)
@@ -26,8 +26,10 @@
             ## Patch up the call to produce nicer result for testing as
             ## try(stop(...)).  This will need adjusting if the
             ## implementation of tryCatch changes.
+            if (inherits(e, "RHSnotFnCall"))
+                call <- "|>"
             ## Use identical() since call[[1L]] can be non-atomic.
-            if (identical(call[[1L]], quote(doTryCatch)))
+            else if (identical(call[[1L]], quote(doTryCatch)))
                 call <- sys.call(-4L)
             dcall <- deparse(call, nlines = 1L)
             prefix <- paste("Error in", dcall, ": ")
```

With behavior:

```
try(parse(text='f|>g'))
# Error in "|>" : 
#   The pipe operator requires a function call as RHS (<text>:1:4)
```

We could consider handling other parseErrors, e.g. `unsupportedInPipe` is also currently pretty unpalatable:

```
try(parse(text = 'f |> `+`(2)'))
# Error in +2 : 
#   function '+' not supported in RHS call of a pipe (<text>:1:6)
```

For now, I'm pausing to keep this thread narrowly focused on the case where `try()` currently errors out before returning, as opposed to returning something odd.
